source_text: Occulta - inquam - tabe carnalis concupiscentiae suae tabificavit in se omnes de sua stirpe venturos
pass_a_gloss: Occulta - inquam - tabe carnal of-desire his-own tabificavit in himself all about/from his-own stirpe venturos.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Augustine reports Julian cited his earlier statement that Adam ‘corrupted in himself everyone to come from his stock,’ as an argument about Christ’s descent from Adam.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
